title: A longer lerp duration buys users adjustment time at the cost of holding the parameter away from its target
content:
A.1.10.3.2.13.2.1.1 states the tension inside the Linear Interpolation Module directly: "A longer `duration` has the benefit of adjusting the parameter more slowly, giving users more time to adjust. However, the drawback of a longer `duration` is that the parameter will not reach its desired `end` value for a longer period of time."

The operative rule follows: "When the cost of a parameter not being at its desired value is high, use of the Linear Interpolation Module is not appropriate, and the parameter should be adjusted to its desired value following the required process."

This is a named boundary on a convenience tool rather than a preference. Gradualism is not free — every day of a long ramp is a day the system knowingly runs at a value it has already judged wrong. The Atlas resolves the conflict by asking which harm dominates: shock to users, or exposure from being off-target.

The consequence for practice is that smoothing is a *risk* decision, not a UX decision, which is why A.1.10.3.2.13.2.1 requires Facilitators to consult the Core Council Risk Advisor before recommending a lerp.
description: Facilitators must weigh both sides; where the cost of an off-target parameter is high, the Atlas rules out interpolation entirely and requires a direct change.
